The cross sections were computed using the Tai formulas, with corrections to the original formulas.
Results are presented for both the random orientation distribution and the horizontal-vertical dipole distribution.
Cross sections are given for 2l/λ ratios between 0.16 and 0.55, and A (2l/a) values up to 4000.
The vertical dipole response is identically zero for all parameter values.
Discontinuities in the fv = 0 column are due to rounding errors and will not significantly impact actual cross section estimates.
In the range 0.19 ≤ 2l/λ ≤ 0.37, the computed cross sections differ from measured values by no more than 1.5 dB on average.
For 2l/λ = 0.5, the measured vertical response is about 1 dB lower than the computed random-distribution response, and the measured horizontal response is 3 dB lower.
The average measured-to-computed response ratio for the random orientation distribution at 2l/λ = 0.5 is -1.8 dB.
Dipoles around 2 inches long do not separate primarily into vertically and horizontally oriented groups, but tend to spiral down at angles near 45°.
The improved accuracy of over 40% compared to the Van Vleck method corresponds to a 50% reduction in the weight of chaff needed to produce a given radar echo.
Experimental tests were conducted on operational chaff, assuming a vertical-horizontal dipole distribution.
The measured cross-section ratio σvv/σhh was used with the tables to estimate the fraction of vertical dipoles (fv).
The ratio of measured-to-computed cross sections had an average value of -1.5 dB ± 1 dB in the range 0.19 ≤ 2l/λ ≤ 0.37.
Neither the random orientation nor the horizontal-vertical distribution completely accounts for the actual measured cross sections.
The tables provide results that are 1.5 dB closer to the measured values than the Van Vleck method.
